clue.text: Head of flight's stuff is found on a plane

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the answer rather than a noun synonym

parts.note: a landing is the level space at the top of a flight of stairs
gear means stuff or belongings

explanation.surface: Someone asks where the pilot's belongings are kept aboard an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' tempts you towards aircraft, but its head here is a staircase's.
explanation.definitionFit: The wheels and struts an aircraft lands on are carried on the plane itself, so the phrase describes the undercarriage.

clue.text: Party member's open-minded to comrade's reform model

parts.note: liberal means tolerant and open-minded

indicators.note: to reform something is to reshape it, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: A political activist is described as tolerant enough to remodel a Communist comrade.
explanation.walkthrough: The Liberal Democrats are a UK political party. 'Model' alone gives T, from Ford's Model T.
explanation.definitionFit: A Liberal Democrat belongs to the British party of that name, so is a member of a political party.

clue.text: Doctor mourns dropping university standards

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so the letters are rearranged
dropping something means letting it go, so a letter is left out

parts.note: taken as written
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Someone laments that academic standards at universities are slipping.
explanation.walkthrough: Take U out of MOURNS, then rearrange what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Norms are the accepted standards or usual patterns of behaviour or quality.

clue.text: Jeopardise prime development on island lake

indicators.note: a development is a change of form, so the letters evolve into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
I is the abbreviation for island
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Building a prime property beside an island lake is said to endanger it.
explanation.definitionFit: To imperil something is to put it in danger, a direct synonym of jeopardise.

clue.text: Escaped with 40% of goods, thanks to wife's agreement

indicators.note: forty percent of a five-letter word is two letters, taken from its front

parts.note: the first two of the word's five letters
ta is British informal for thanks
W is the abbreviation for wife
ay (aye) is a word of agreement, yes

explanation.surface: A thief escapes with part of the loot, thanks to the wife's consent.
explanation.walkthrough: Ta is everyday British slang for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: To get away is to escape, so the past tense matches escaped.

clue.text: I see said vision

indicators.note: said means spoken out loud, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: the letter I is pronounced like the organ of sight
to sight something is to see it

explanation.surface: Someone says 'I see' while talking about their vision.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight is the faculty of seeing, which is what vision means.

clue.text: Putin regime's inner circle time and time again taking drug — it's a dangerous game

indicators.note: something inner sits inside, so a letter is placed within the regime's words

parts.note: the Russian president's regime is Russian rule
a circle has the shape of the letter O
T is the abbreviation for time, here given twice
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: The Kremlin's inner circle keeps returning to drugs, a risky pursuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inner circle' reads as a single phrase for Putin's advisers, but the circle goes inside RUSSIAN RULE.
explanation.definitionFit: Russian roulette is the deadly gamble of spinning a revolver loaded with one bullet and firing at one's own head.

clue.text: Espy original child within the inner self

indicators.note: within means inside, so one piece is placed in the middle of another
original suggests something newly created, so the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
CH is the abbreviation for child

explanation.surface: A psychologist claims to glimpse the original inner child within the self.
explanation.definitionFit: The psyche is the human soul or mind, the inner self as opposed to the body.

clue.text: Joins college climbing club

parts.note: uni is short for university, a college

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a set is a social group or club

explanation.surface: A student joins a university mountaineering society.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite things is to bring them together, so unites is a synonym of joins.

clue.text: Old boy has clean turned around after direction to stop drinking

indicators.note: after places the old boy's letters behind the direction in the chain

parts.note: S for south, a compass direction
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: turning around means facing back the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: pure means clean or unsullied

explanation.surface: An old boy has turned his life around, cleaning up and quitting alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: To sober up is to recover from being drunk, so it suits giving up drink.

clue.text: Yorkshireman declared the motive for treachery

indicators.note: how a Yorkshireman says the words out loud is what matters, in his dialect

parts.note: Yorkshire speech clips the to t', and a motive is a reason

explanation.surface: A man from Yorkshire announces why someone betrayed their country.
explanation.walkthrough: In Yorkshire dialect (northern England), 'the' is famously shortened to t', so 'the reason' becomes t'reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is the crime of betraying one's country, a form of treachery.

clue.text: Irish city's team get together for opening drink

definitions.note: describes the tool's purpose rather than naming it

parts.note: Cork is a city in southern Ireland, with the possessive s
a crew is a team of people gathered to work together

explanation.surface: A team from Cork meets up for a first drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Cork is the Republic of Ireland's second city.
explanation.definitionFit: A corkscrew is the spiral tool used to pull corks from wine bottles, letting you open a drink.

clue.text: Wally and I do it all over the place

indicators.note: something all over the place is scattered and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone admits that they and a hapless friend both make a mess of things.
explanation.walkthrough: Wally is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A wally, in British slang, is a silly or foolish person, which is what an idiot is.

clue.text: Anyone else having a piece of fish?

indicators.note: a piece of something is a fragment, so the letters are found inside the words

parts.note: letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A host at a fish supper asks if anyone else wants some.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are long snake-like fish, so they are examples of fish.

clue.text: Theatre props for kids?

parts.note: surface reading: the objects used on stage during a performance
setter's reading: objects children play with, toys

explanation.walkthrough: A theatre's props are, literally, things used in plays; the question mark flags that children's play is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Toys are objects children play with, so the stage term doubles as a word for them.

clue.text: Live more recklessly and cause confusion!

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
wilder means more uncontrolled or reckless

explanation.surface: An exhortation to live dangerously and stir up chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: To bewilder someone is to puzzle or perplex them, so it causes confusion.

clue.text: He knows all about crank detective

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
a crank is a lever-like arm for turning
dick is old slang for a detective

explanation.surface: A sleuth is said to be an expert in eccentric detectives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knows all about' looks like one phrase, but 'about' belongs to the wordplay. Clever dick is British slang for a know-all.
explanation.definitionFit: A clever dick is a smug know-it-all, someone who thinks he knows everything.

clue.text: Doctor wearing jacket in battle

indicators.note: someone wearing a garment is inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a coat is an outer jacket
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A medic in a jacket goes into combat.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor here is a person, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Combat is fighting between armed forces, a synonym of battle.

clue.text: Most ridiculous fellow's supporting lawyer on trial

indicators.note: in a down clue, what supports sits underneath, so the fellow comes below the lawyer

parts.note: a DA is a district attorney, an American prosecutor
F is the abbreviation for fellow
a trial is a test

explanation.surface: An absurd defendant backs his lawyer through a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: Daft means silly, so the superlative daftest means the most ridiculous.

clue.text: Cold going into pick treat from the freezer!

indicators.note: going into means entering, so a letter is put inside the other word

parts.note: a pick is a choice
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone shivers while choosing a frozen dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: A choc ice is a British bar of ice cream coated in chocolate.
explanation.definitionFit: A choc ice is a chocolate-covered ice-cream bar kept frozen, so it is a frozen treat.

clue.text: Catcall gives start to blue tit

parts.note: boo is a jeer from an audience

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the colour word

explanation.surface: A jeer at a blue tit, the garden bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue tit' is a common British bird, but 'tit' is slang for breast here.
explanation.definitionFit: Both tit and boob are vulgar slang words for a woman's breast.

clue.text: Insect eats son and one daughter to get by

indicators.note: something eaten ends up inside the eater, so letters go within the insect

parts.note: a bee is an insect
S is the abbreviation for son
I is the Roman numeral one
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: An insect feeds on a family's children just to survive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get by' looks like 'survive', but 'by' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: By and beside both mean next to, as in a house by the sea.

clue.text: Mum takes gold kiwi back from New Zealand

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the bird's name

explanation.surface: A mother brings a kiwi fruit or bird home from New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: Or is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Maori, as an adjective, describes the indigenous Polynesian people of New Zealand and their culture.

clue.text: Disgusting loo's filth is found at the bottom of mountains

definitions.text: found at the bottom of mountains
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the answer rather than a plain noun

indicators.note: something disgusting is foul or messed up, so the letters are put in disarray

parts.note: taken as written, including the s

explanation.surface: A grimy toilet is discovered at the base of a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: Foothills are the low hills lying at the base of a mountain range.

clue.text: Eastern city's hospital has a new oxygen unit

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
a unit is one, the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A hospital in an Asian city opens a new oxygen ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanoi is the capital of Vietnam, a city in East Asia.

clue.text: Cut short a game

parts.note: taken as written
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A match ends early.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a book or speech is to shorten it, cutting it down.

clue.text: Inflamed by the stress of dieting

indicators.note: stress pulls something out of shape, so the letters are distorted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is made irritable by the strain of a diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflamed literally means set on fire, so ignited is a synonym.

clue.text: Reverse the flow of events — Canute couldn't

definitions.meaning: first meaning: change the course of a situation

definitions.note: describes what the king failed to do rather than naming it
definitions.meaning: second meaning: what the king famously failed to do to the sea

explanation.walkthrough: King Canute (Cnut), an 11th-century ruler of England, is said to have sat on the shore commanding the sea to retreat, and failed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to reverse a trend, and literally means to make the sea go back, which the legend says Canute could not.
